! We have discussed this ticket a bit on today's tech call. We think we could do this without too much trouble, but we wanted to check with you to understand the need a bit better. Are you trying to negotiate capabilities with your Fedora instances? Are you trying to understand whether a given interaction can successfully begin or complete?

As you've probably noticed, we want to push folks as much as possible towards a REST HATEOS style of interaction, which implies discovering capabilities as part of HTTP interactions. So we want to make sure that you have a way to do what you need to do that doesn't depend on anything as fragile as parsing build numbers or the like.

Our need is actually fairly simple.  When certain activities happen in our application, we want to be able to log the version of Fedora we were using at the time, without having to parse it out of an HTML page.  Let me know if you need further information.
, In other words, the recent patch will not suit your needs?

That would not be our preferred means of retrieving the version information.  Retrieving and parsing an HTML page for data seems a bit brittle.  On the other hand, this isn't a deal breaker for us by any means.  if we are the only ones who care about this functionality, there are undoubtedly higher priority issues for fcrepo developers to be working on.

There is not an integration test for this because Grizzly simply removes the Server header and replaces it with its own value, but this has been manually tested in both Jetty and Tomcat. Either way, given the principle of HATEOS, a client should not rely on this value, especially since proxy servers are often wont to strip out a Server header.
This looks good, but the integration tests in fcrepo-http-api need help.
I am closing the PR I proposed for this – it seems that the best approach would be to push this functionality into an extension module. I would be fine with closing the ticket as "Won't Fix".
Thanks for giving this a try. An extension module or not, I suspect Fedora clients will often times want to know which version of Fedora they are working against.
Fedora 5 is unsupported for new features. This feature is available in Fedora 6.x

Fedora 3 provided an API method ('describe') which would return the Fedora software version number (among other things).  As near as I can tell, Fedora 4 only reports the version number in HTML (on the top level /fcrepo page).  It would be good to be able to get the version number via an API call as in Fedora 3.

comments.body: Nianli Ma, it would be good to add the same version information that is found in the root HTML page as RDF triples on the rest/ endpoint. We can discuss the exact predicates that would make sense.

Esmé Cowles? Nick Ruest? A. Soroka? others? We would like to create three new triples on the repository root:
<root> <p0> <release#>
<root> <p1> <build#>
<root> <p2> <build-date>

Note: This is the same information that is presently rendered at the bottom-right of the root HTML page:
http://demo.fcrepo.org:8080/fcrepo/

Do you have any suggestions for what appropriate predicates (p0, p1, and p2) may be?
No idea. fedora:yourFlavorOfPain?

Andrew Woods

Are these new predicates for the Fedora ontology?

I found this: The Software Ontology http://theswo.sourceforge.net/ – I can't find the ontology published anywhere, but:

  • versionName – could be releaseNumber
  • don't see anything for buildNumber or buildDate

An aside, has JIRA changed? It took me to a new page to reply.

—

A. Soroka skos:related Dinosaur Jr.
There was a small change to JIRA today that removed the option to create a login via JIRA directly, but that does not sound related to what you are seeing.

Another option would be to use DOAP: http://usefulinc.com/ns/doap#

</> doap:release </#release>
</#release> a doap:Version;
doap:name "build 1234";
doap:created "2015-11-12";
doap:revision "4.4.4" .

I had forgotten about DOAP. Apache uses DOAP. +1 to DOAP.

DOAP DOAP DOAP!
...and it gives us a chance to eat our own hash-food. +1, Thanks Esmé Cowles.
And if DOAP is, well, dope, we could also add some triples describing the project to the root too.
Sounds good to me!
